title: Printed before the result was clear.
description:
Printed before the result was clear. The Chicago Tribune, 3 November 1948, the morning after the US presidential election. The first edition went to press while only early returns were in.

A strike moved the deadline. Printers were on strike, so the first edition had to be finished hours earlier than usual, according to the Library of Congress and WBEZ.

Early returns showed Dewey ahead. The paper's political correspondent assured the editor that Dewey was in, and the editor ordered the presses to roll.

Over 150,000 copies were already on the street when the Tribune had second thoughts. Trucks were sent out to collect them.

Truman won by more than two million votes. The popular vote was 24,105,812 to 21,970,065, according to the Library of Congress.

On his way back to Washington, he was handed a copy and held it up for the photographers, grinning broadly.

The deadline was real. The certainty was not.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewey_Defeats_Truman: read in full. Established the headline ran on 3 November 1948, the day after the election, that some 150,000 copies had been printed before correction, that the paper went to press before most results were in, and that Truman held up a copy for photographers. Its account of the strike, the Washington correspondent and the 303 to 189 to 39 electoral vote was not used because other sources could not confirm it.
- https://blogs.loc.gov/loc/2012/11/stop-the-presses/: read in full (Library of Congress blog, 6 November 2012). Established that a printers' strike forced editors to go to press hours before the normal time, that the Library holds a copy dated 3 November 1948, and the popular vote of 24,105,812 for Truman to 21,970,065 for Dewey.
- https://www.wbez.org/stories/the-tribune-messes-upor-what-ever-happened-to-president-dewey/8a765b9a-7b6a-4d08-af0b-d38cd797e002: read in full (WBEZ, John R. Schmidt). Established that printers were on strike so the first edition had an earlier deadline, that first returns showed Dewey ahead, that the political correspondent assured the editor Dewey was in, that over 150,000 papers were on the street, that trucks were sent to retrieve them, and that Truman held up a copy for photographers, grinning broadly.
- https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/30749/what-made-people-think-dewey-defeated-truman: read in full (Mental Floss, 23 May 2012). Corroborated the strike, the earlier press time, the 150,000 copies and that Truman was handed a copy as he travelled back to Washington.
